refs efcore saving/transactions.md:17 "By default, if the database provider supports transactions, all changes in a single call to `SaveChanges` are applied in a transaction. If any of the changes fail, then the transaction is rolled back and none of the changes are applied to the database."

PostgreSQL 17, 13.2.1 (WebFetch, quoted block): "Read Committed is the default isolation level in PostgreSQL. When a transaction uses this isolation level, a SELECT query (without a FOR UPDATE/SHARE clause) sees only data committed before the query began". Capture order-history.txt line 13 shows both rows right after `cancel -> 200`.

refs efcore saving/related-data.md:28 "If you reference a new entity from the navigation property of an entity that is already tracked by the context, the entity will be discovered and inserted"; :36 "If you change the navigation property of an entity, the corresponding changes will be made to the foreign key column in the database." Execution: capture order-history.txt shows the new order's `placed` row found by `WHERE order_id = $order`, i.e. order_id was filled for an order created in the same save.

OrdersController.cs:83-95: `[HttpGet("{id:int}/history")]`, `var order = await repository.FindForReadingAsync(id); if (order is null) return NotFound();`, `AuthorizeAsync(User, order, "OrderOwner")` -> `Forbid()`, then `history.ListAsync(id)` mapped to `OrderStatusChangeDto(c.Event, c.Status, c.OccurredAt)`. EfOrderRepository.cs:15-16 FindForReadingAsync uses `AsNoTracking()`.

EfOrderHistory.cs:12-17: `db.OrderStatusHistory.Where(row => row.OrderId == orderId).OrderBy(row => row.Id).Select(row => new OrderStatusChange(row.Event, row.Status, row.OccurredAt)).ToListAsync();` id is an identity column (migration: IdentityByDefaultColumn), so Id order is insertion order.

refs efcore querying/tracking.md:67 "If the result set doesn't contain any entity types, then no tracking is done. In the following query, we return an anonymous type with some of the values from the entity (but no instances of the actual entity type). There are no tracked entities coming out of the query." OrderStatusChange is a record of three scalars (OrderStatusChange.cs:6), not an entity type.

Migration Up (AddOrderStatusHistory.cs:47-50): `INSERT INTO order_status_history (order_id, event, status, occurred_at) SELECT id, 'placed', 'new', placed_at FROM orders ORDER BY id`. Verified as to what the migration writes. 'Nothing else is recoverable' holds for orders but not absolutely: the stage-2 notifications table kept order_id, subject ('order placed', ...) and created_at per email job (see claim 2).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Migration AddOrderStatusHistory backfills one row per existing order: 'placed', 'new', orders.placed_at. orders holds nothing else about earlier changes, so nothing else can be rebuilt from it.
